title: Integrating Omics and CRISPR Technology for Identification and Verification of Genomic Safe Harbor Loci in the Chicken Genome
author: Dehdilani, Goshayeshi, et al.
materials: DF1 cells were grown in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium/Nutrient Mixture F-12 (DMEM/F12) (Gibco, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (Gibco, USA), and penicillin (10,000 I.U./mL)/streptomycin (10,000 μg/mL) (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). To achieve stable heterogenous EGFP-expressing cell pools, VH, VR, VO, ΔVH, ΔVR, and ΔVO targeting vectors (1ug/ul from each) along with the corresponding specific Cas9/gRNA vectors (1 ug/ul from each) were co-transfected into the DF1 cells (2 × 105 cells per 12 well-plate) using Lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen, USA) in six different experimental groups (in three biological replicates). These groups included cells with CMV-driven EGFP and ΔCMV-driven EGFP in three loci of cHIPP, cROSA, and cOVA (Additional file 7B, C). Transfection was followed by a 1-week selection with 1 μg/mL of puromycin (Sigma-Aldrich, USA) and another week for recovery (Additional file 7A). At the end of month two (MTH2), the heterogeneous cell pools carrying DsRed2-ΔCMV-EGFP in each of the three loci were subjected to limiting dilution to achieve the isogenous cell clones that stably expressed EGFP (Additional file 7C). At the end of months four (MTH4) and six (MTH6), each group of long-term cultured isogenous cell clones was evaluated for EGFP and DsRed2 expression (Additional file 7D, E). We reasoned that any possible DsRed2 expression without any promoter may indicate the influence of the genomic context in the relevant GSH locus. To make control groups, the sgRNA-free Cas9 (-gRNA) vector (1 ug/ul) was co-transfected with each of the VH, VR, VO, ΔVH, ΔVR, and ΔVO (1ug/ul from each) targeting vectors. The expression of EGFP and DsRed2 was assessed in heterogenous cell pools at the end of MTH2 (Additional file 7B and 7C), and in isogenous cell clones isolated from the long-term culture (> 2 months) of heterogenous cell pools at the end of MTH4 (Additional file 7D) and MTH6 (Additional file 7E).

The images captured from each group of heterogeneous cell pools (containing either CMV or ΔCMV promoter) were analyzed by ImageJ Fiji software (version 1.52p) to calculate the integrity density index. For this purpose, cells were imaged with identical parameters (for images from CMV groups: 10X magnification, 100 µs exposure, 1X analog gain, and for images from ΔCMV groups: 20X magnification, 1 s exposure, 2.2X analog gain). Also, isogenous cell clones containing ΔCMV promoter were analyzed to calculate the integrity density index. These cells were also imaged with identical parameters (20X magnification, 1 s exposure, 1X analog gain). The integrity density index was further analyzed by GNUastro Linux-based software (version 0.18) for images taken from isogenous cell lines containing ΔCMV promoter (Additional file 11).

Total protein was extracted from isogenous cell clones carrying DsRed2- ΔCMV-EGFP using RIPA lysis buffer (Cytomatin gene, Iran). Briefly, 50 µl RIPA lysis buffer was poured on the cells cultured in a 0.35 cm2 cell culture dish after removing the culture medium, followed by 30 min incubation in a minus 30 freezer. Then, cells were scraped and centrifuged in 4 °C with a speed of 13,000 rpm for 5 min. Total protein was collected from the supernatant and stored at a minus 80 freezer. The BCA protein assay was conducted to determine the concentration of total protein. Each protein sample (30 μg) was subjected to 10% SDS-PAGE, transferred onto 0.45 µm nitrocellulose membrane (Biorad, USA) according to the standard protocol, followed by blocking (overnight at 4 °C) with 5% w/v skim milk prepared in D-PBS. The membrane was incubated with rabbit monoclonal antibody (Sino Biological Inc., China) against EGFP (1:2000) for 3 h at room temperature, and with HRP-conjugated goat anti-rabbit secondary antibody (1/18000) (Abcam, UK) for 1 h at room temperature. As an internal control, chicken β-actin protein was used to normalize the results. To this end, stripping of the same membrane was performed using a standard protocol and blocking was conducted with 5% skim milk overnight at 4 °C. Then, the membrane was subjected to a mouse monoclonal anti-β-actin antibody (1/20000) (Sigma Aldrich, USA) for 1 h at room temperature. Throughout the experiments, each membrane was washed three times (15 min per wash) using TBST solution. Finally, in order to detect the HRP signals, membranes were subjected to chemiluminescence detection with the Chemiluminescence Kit (Parstous, Iran), and the Chemiluminescence Detector system (G: BOX Chemi XT Analyser, SYNGENE, Eur.). The ImageJ software was used for densitometric analysis of the EGFP (27 kilodalton) and chicken β-actin (42 kilodalton) protein bands. Mean relative intensity was calculated and Mann–Whitney test was used to compare the relative intensity among the analyzed groups (p < 0.05).

steps.title: Amplify homology arms
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from DF1 cells and PCR‑amplify the 5′ and 3′ homology arm (HA) sequences flanking each sgRNA target site using the primer sets listed (P1‑P4 for cROSA left HA, P5‑P8 for cROSA right HA, P9‑P10 for cHIPP left HA, P11‑P12 for cHIPP right HA, P13‑P16 for cOVA left HA, P17‑P20 for cOVA right HA).

steps.title: Construct targeting vectors
steps.instruction: Sub‑clone each pair of amplified HA fragments into the PvuI/XhoI and NheI/XcmI sites of the DsRed2‑PolyA‑CMV‑EGFP‑IRES‑PACr‑PolyA backbone to generate the cROSA (VR), cHIPP (VH), and cOVA (VO) targeting vectors. Create weakened‑promoter versions (ΔVH, ΔVR, ΔVO) by removing the distal CMV segment from BglII to SnaBI, yielding DsRed2‑PolyA‑ΔCMV‑EGFP‑IRES‑PACr‑PolyA cassettes.

steps.title: Clone sgRNA oligos
steps.instruction: Design sgRNA oligonucleotides (cROSA: 5’-tccgggtcggtttggcccct-3’, cHIPP: 5’-gcctgtactttgttagtgac-3’, cOVA: 5’-gctctagccatggtatacct-3’) with CHOPCHOP, anneal them, and ligate into the BbsI sites downstream of the U6 promoter in the CBA‑Cas9‑T2A‑PACr vector. All vectors retain the puromycin‑resistance gene (PACr).

steps.title: Culture DF1 cells
steps.instruction: Maintain DF1 chicken embryonic fibroblast cells in DMEM/F12 (Gibco) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco), penicillin 10 000 IU · mL⁻¹ and streptomycin 10 000 µg · mL⁻¹ (Thermo Fisher).

steps.title: Co‑transfect targeting constructs
steps.instruction: Seed 2 × 10⁵ DF1 cells per well of a 12‑well plate. For each of the six experimental groups (VH, VR, VO, ΔVH, ΔVR, ΔVO) co‑transfect 1 µg · µL⁻¹ of the appropriate targeting vector together with 1 µg · µL⁻¹ of its corresponding Cas9/sgRNA vector using Lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Include control wells where the sgRNA‑free Cas9 vector (1 µg · µL⁻¹) is co‑transfected with each targeting vector.

steps.title: Select and recover transfected cells
steps.instruction: Begin puromycin selection 24 h post‑transfection by adding 1 µg · mL⁻¹ puromycin (Sigma‑Aldrich) to the medium for 1 week, then replace with fresh medium and allow a 1‑week recovery period.

steps.title: Isolate isogenic clones
steps.instruction: At two months post‑transfection (MTH2), perform limiting‑dilution cloning of the heterogeneous pools carrying DsRed2‑ΔCMV‑EGFP to obtain single‑cell derived isogenic clones that stably express EGFP. Continue culturing clones and evaluate EGFP and DsRed2 expression at four months (MTH4) and six months (MTH6).

steps.title: Capture fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Image heterogeneous pools and isogenic clones under identical microscope settings: for CMV‑driven groups use 10× magnification, 100 µs exposure, 1× analog gain; for ΔCMV groups use 20× magnification, 1 s exposure, 2.2× analog gain (isogenic clones imaged at 20×, 1 s exposure, 1× gain).

steps.title: Analyze image density
steps.instruction: Process the acquired images with ImageJ Fiji (v1.52p) to calculate the integrity density index, then further analyse the ΔCMV isogenic‑clone images using GNUastro (v0.18) on Linux.

steps.title: Extract total protein
steps.instruction: Remove medium from cells grown in a 0.35 cm² dish, add 50 µL RIPA lysis buffer (Cytomatin gene, Iran), and incubate on ice at –30 °C for 30 min. Scrape cells, centrifuge at 13 000 rpm, 4 °C for 5 min, collect supernatant, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Quantify and prepare samples
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration with a BCA assay. Mix 30 µg of each sample with loading buffer and denature as required for SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer
steps.instruction: Separate proteins on a 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel, then transfer onto a 0.45 µm nitrocellulose membrane (Bio‑Rad) following standard protocols.

steps.title: Probe for EGFP
steps.instruction: Block the membrane overnight at 4 °C with 5 % (w/v) skim milk in D‑PBS. Incubate with rabbit monoclonal anti‑EGFP antibody (1:2000, Sino Biological) for 3 h at room temperature, wash, then incubate with HRP‑conjugated goat anti‑rabbit secondary antibody (1:18000, Abcam) for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Strip and probe for β‑actin
steps.instruction: Strip the membrane using a standard stripping buffer, re‑block overnight at 4 °C with 5 % skim milk, then incubate with mouse monoclonal anti‑β‑actin antibody (1:20000, Sigma‑Aldrich) for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash and detect signals
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane three times with TBST (15 min each wash). Develop chemiluminescence using the Parstous Chemiluminescence Kit (Iran) and capture images with the G: BOX Chemi XT Analyzer (SYNGENE).

steps.title: Quantify band intensities
steps.instruction: Use ImageJ to perform densitometric analysis of the EGFP (27 kDa) and chicken β‑actin (42 kDa) bands, calculate mean relative intensities, and apply the Mann–Whitney test for statistical comparison (p < 0.05).
